intro.text: A Tukari caravan in Shadesmar that camped at Nameless and turned away anyone who approached, keeping to itself.
A band of Tukari mercenaries in Shadesmar, more than twenty strong and led by a man in a blue-on-yellow overcoat, who hunted down and attacked the honorspren Notum.

description.text: At least one of them speaks rough Alethi; the rest speak Tukari.

They travel without pack animals. At rest, they heap their belongings in the middle of camp, where people take turns sleeping under guard. They carry cudgels and, out of sight, cutlasses; a few have shields, but none seem to have armor or bows.
Their camp feels unwelcoming and eerie, as if everything, the Tukari included, lies in shadow and their faces are hard to make out. They keep it unlit even though they have manifested fire.

Both men and women have brown skin and black hair. Their clothes follow the fashion of southeastern Makabak: Azish colors and patterns, but in heavier, rougher cloth that covers more of the body, with braided tassels at the waist.

items.text: In 1175 the caravan stopped at Nameless while the honorspren Notum was visiting. When Adolin and Godeke came to learn about them, the Tukari quickly sent them off, preferring to keep apart from everyone else in the town.

For weeks the Tukari followed Adolin's group, always staying several hours behind. Thinking his party was their target, Adolin had soldiers keep watch on them, and every messenger he sent to them was turned back.

About a day from Lasting Integrity, the Tukari turned south after Notum's patrol. When they caught up, some of them attacked him and his Reacher companions with torches, swords and spears, tied up the spren and stabbed him again and again, hoping enough pain would break his mind and kill him.
Realizing the caravan had never been after his own group, Adolin rode ahead with Maya to help Notum while the others followed, and took on the mercenaries alone to buy time.

Losing six in Adolin's first charge shook the Tukari, and many shied away, which he pressed to his advantage until their captain organized them against him. One of them ran a spear through Adolin's stomach.
Once Maya joined the fight, the Tukari grew afraid to attack. Their leader urged them on, but after a few more died, some fled back toward the rest of the caravan.
The leader's bodyguard went for Adolin, who dodged him and struck the leader on the shoulder. The remaining fighters broke and retreated to their caravan, which then left the area.
Fearing another attack, Adolin's group pushed on to reach Lasting Integrity and the honorspren's protection by the end of the day.
